rows.title: Cleanup verification generation/PID-reuse safe
rows.evidence: Iteration 5 (delta F6): typed CleanupVerification landed (ConfirmedAbsent{basis}/StillPresent{survivors}/Indeterminate{reason}/Unsupported{reason}, closed enum, typed evidence payloads; a sent signal is never a basis). Child leads its own process group (setpgid(0,0) in the trusted pre-exec sequence; failure = typed PreExecStage::ProcessGroup), so a reaped run probes kill(-pgid,0) and an unobserved death probes pid+start_time+boot_id. PID-reuse safe: alive-but-different start time => ConfirmedAbsent{IdentityMismatch}; boot change => ConfirmedAbsent{BootIdChanged} (checked before any probe); unreadable start time => Indeterminate, never a proof of absence; targets <= 1 refused before the syscall. Only ConfirmedAbsent records CleanupConfirmed; duplicate verification refused by the state machine. ActivatedSandbox::stop kills the group (and the child pid, for a setsid escapee) and reports the waitpid observation; StopError::SignalFailed is typed. Live-proven on macOS: verify-after-exit, honest StillPresent for a backgrounded grandchild then ConfirmedAbsent after the consumer kills the group, stop()-then-verify, stopped-before-activation verify; removing setpgid makes the survivor test report ConfirmedAbsent while /bin/sleep 30 still runs. 17 unit + 5 live tests. Pending: recovered-session verification (needs the durable store, R09); Linux verification (R07 blocker); documented dark spot - a descendant that calls setsid leaves the group (needs a cgroup-class mechanism).
